title: Sustaining China’s leadership in metabolic research: NSFC funding growth, equity challenges, and policy imperatives
content: Over the past few decades, China has emerged as a global leader in scientific and technological innovation, driven by a strategic emphasis on fundamental research. A pivotal factor underpinning this progress is the substantial increase in research funding, enabled by the nation’s sustained economic growth and the rapid expansion of its scientific workforce. The Chinese government has systematically prioritized research and development (R&D), consistently elevating its investment as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP). According to recent statistics, China’s R&D expenditure now accounts for nearly 2.5% of its GDP (as of 2022), with a growing proportion allocated to foundational scientific inquiries.
